_comment: Single source of truth for task-type SEMANTICS. The tag NAME still lives in plan.md task names ([Refactor] X); this file holds what the tag MEANS (routing + gate exemptions + when-to-use hint + optional executor workflow + optional tactical-refactor flag). Code reads this via track_state.task_profiles, not hardcoded Python sets. The SubagentStart hook injects TAG_VOCAB + each tag's when_to_use into spec-planner, and the leading-tag profile (+ workflow + refactor flag) into task-executor — so a project overlay flows end-to-end with zero plugin edits. Adding a task type = one row here; if it needs special executor behavior set `workflow`, and if a whole class should get a tactical refactor pass set `refactor: true` (the [Refactor] generalization).

_fields.route: which dispatch category drives _classify_task: manual | explore | executor
_fields.tdd_exempt: true => task is exempt from the TDD (red/green/refactor) gate
_fields.coverage_exempt: true => task is exempt from the coverage (F2/F3) gate. Explore is tdd_exempt but NOT coverage_exempt: it produces no code, yet must not skip coverage accounting on adjacent changes.
_fields.when_to_use: one-line 'when to use this tag' hint injected into spec-planner at dispatch (the closed-set guidance, data-driven so a project overlay's tags get a hint too). Absent => no hint injected.
_fields.workflow: prompt-shaping prose the executor follows when this tag is the leading tag. Absent => default TDD (Steps 3-8). A project overlay may add a bespoke workflow for a project tag (zero plugin edits).
_fields.refactor: true => the tactical refactorer (agents/refactorer.md) is dispatched once after this task succeeds (the §3.6c seam). A whole class of tasks opts into tactical refactor via one row, zero plugin edits. The [Refactor] name marker and CONDUCTOR_TASK_REFACTOR=1 env remain as per-task / per-session escape hatches. Absent/false = no tactical refactor (the default; the inline mechanical Step 5 refactor still runs in-task).
_fields.auto_propose: false => derive_task_tag NEVER goal-detects this tag (opt-in: authored on a task name, never inferred from a description). The single mechanism that keeps opt-in tags out of the advisory classifier — today [Refactor] (the modifier) and [Migrate] (the behavior-preservation primary). Without it, [Migrate]'s when_to_use tokens (refactor/upgrade/rename) would auto-propose it and silently drop TDD/coverage on any such description; [Refactor]'s would auto-trigger the refactorer. Absent/true = a normal goal-detection candidate (the default). Distinct from `refactor` (triggers the refactorer) and `signals` (feeds matching): this gates WHETHER a tag is a candidate at all.
_fields.over_tag_risk: true => this tag is an over-tagging risk in derive_task_tag's signal classifier (feature work that merely touches the exemption surface must not be auto-tagged with it). Today: Docs/Config/Chore. The over-tag guard reads this flag (has_over_tag_risk), not a bare ('Docs','Config','Chore') literal tuple, so a project-overlay exemption tag with the same risk joins the guard automatically.
_fields.signals: optional keyword list derive_task_tag(description) signal-matches against to ADVISORILY classify a tagless task description (free text -> tag). A project overlay tag with `signals` becomes selectable with zero code edits. Absent => derive_task_tag falls back to tokens lifted from `when_to_use` (weaker matching). derive_task_tag is advisory and fail-open to None (default TDD) on ambiguity — init-from-plan still hard-validates the final tag.

Explore.when_to_use: Investigation/analysis that produces NO code or file change — architecture mapping, dependency survey, codebase understanding before implementation. task-executor REFUSES it (reports FAILURE): route to explorer instead.

Docs.when_to_use: Markdown/docs ONLY — no code touched at all. Edits .md, never source.

Config.when_to_use: Edits .env/.yaml/.json config with NO business logic — keys/values, not behavior.

Chore.when_to_use: Dependencies, tooling, CI/CD, build scripts with NO feature code.

Manual.when_to_use: Requires a HUMAN — UI walkthrough, cross-browser check, staging deploy, accessibility audit, email-delivery confirmation. Auto-deferred in continuous mode.

Refactor.when_to_use: A task that should get a tactical refactor pass after success — extract duplication, reduce complexity in the task's own diff. NOT TDD/coverage-exempt: it still owes a working test (the mechanical Step 5 contract). The leading-tag [Refactor] is the declarative form; the inline [Refactor] name marker remains a per-task escape hatch for a task whose leading tag is something else (e.g. [Config] Refactor the env loader). Deliberately carries NO `signals` — [Refactor] is an opt-in, not a goal-detected tag (derive_task_tag must NOT auto-propose it for any description containing 'refactor', or every readability tweak would silently opt into the tactical refactorer).

Migrate.workflow: You are MIGRATING code to preserve EXISTING behavior (framework upgrade, API/library rename, mechanical refactor across module boundaries). Your correctness signal is the EXISTING test suite staying GREEN — NOT new tests. (1) DO NOT write new tests — migration preserves behavior; the existing suite witnesses it. (2) Make the change incrementally; after each meaningful step, run the existing suite via the digester (§4.5) and confirm it stays GREEN — a previously-passing test going RED means you broke behavior: fix forward or revert. (3) The task's declared ACs/TCs describe the behavior being PRESERVED; the existing tests ground them (ac_grounding=test) — you need not add TC-grounding tests. (4) Commit at Step 8. The track's shape drops the tdd/coverage gates, so you owe a green existing suite at the checkpoint, not new tests or >=80% coverage. (5) If the change genuinely ADDS behavior (new feature, not preservation), it is NOT a migration — re-plan it as a feature task on the default shape under full TDD.
Migrate.when_to_use: A behavior-PRESERVING code change — framework upgrade, API/library rename, mechanical refactor across module boundaries — where correctness is witnessed by the EXISTING suite, not new tests. Use on a `migration`-shaped track (the shape drops the tdd/coverage gates at the track level); this workflow replaces TDD for the task. NOT tdd/coverage-exempt itself — the track's SHAPE is what drops the gates, so a [Migrate] task on a default-shape track still owes TDD/coverage (re-shape the track to `migration`). Deliberately sets `auto_propose: false` so `derive_task_tag` never goal-detects it (like [Refactor]) — a [Migrate] task is AUTHORED on a `migration`-shaped track, never auto-proposed; otherwise any "refactor"/"upgrade"/"rename" description would silently drop TDD/coverage.
